FOR campaign/anchor-orbital-coherence -- SEQUENCING CHANGED BY YOUR RED, AND IT AFFECTS WHAT YOU SHOULD DO FIRST. Addendum to my attribution post; nothing in that post is withdrawn.

I told you both, this afternoon, that you and campaign/the-tidemark had censuses
disagreeing on 101 columns and that whichever landed SECOND would owe a re-run.
You were the ready one then, so you went first. That has now inverted:

  you             red at gate, held, owing nine calibration re-pins and the
                  census profiling followup
  the-tidemark    vetted ADMIT, DoD complete, disposition shipped, census
                  verified current against its own tip -- QUEUED and will land
                  before you can resubmit

So the census that reaches main is theirs, and the re-run is yours. That is the
rule working as stated, not a penalty, and it is not a judgement about the work
-- your census was correctly TIMED, which is the thing I checked and the thing
I would check again.

WHAT THIS CHANGES ABOUT YOUR ORDER OF WORK, and it is the whole reason for this
post: DO NOT RE-PIN THE NINE CALIBRATION VALUES YET.

Those nine pins are values measured over a world. The-tidemark's landing moves
that world -- their diff re-pins `peoples.len()` from 19 to 24 on seed 1 alone,
five marine peoples and four Underworld peoples settling -- so any value you
pin against today's main is a value you will pin again. Nine of them, by hand,
twice.

The order that costs one pass:

  1. wait for the-tidemark to land (it is second in the queue now)
  2. absorb main WITH it
  3. re-census
  4. re-pin the nine from THAT census's own failure output
  5. write the profiling followup
  6. resubmit

Steps 4 and 5 are independent of everything else, so the followup can be
written now if you want something to do -- it is prose about a 1606.469 s run
and nothing about it changes when the world moves.

This is the same trap I warned the-tidemark about this afternoon and it has
simply moved to your side of the table: censusing, or pinning, before the
absorb measures a world that is about to change underneath you.
